units.title: Lipschitz growth bounds every supplied subgradient
units.statement: For any globally G-Lipschitz real-valued function on a real inner-product space, every global supporting vector v at x satisfies ‖v‖≤G.
assumptions: E is a real inner-product space with its associated norm. No completeness or finite-dimensionality assumption is imposed.
G is a nonnegative real Lipschitz constant and f:E→ℝ is globally G-Lipschitz.
SupportsAt f x v means f(x)+⟨v,z−x⟩≤f(z) for every z∈E. It supplies a genuine global supporting vector; no differentiability or totalized gradient is used.

steps.title: Probe in the supporting direction
steps.text: Evaluate the global supporting inequality at z=x+v. The pairing is exactly ‖v‖², with no derivative or inverse norm needed.

steps.title: Use the actual Lipschitz bound
steps.text: The function increment is at most its absolute value, and global Lipschitz continuity bounds that absolute value by G‖v‖.

steps.title: Keep the zero vector separate
steps.text: If v=0 the result is nonnegativity of G. Otherwise ‖v‖>0, so the quadratic inequality implies ‖v‖≤G. This is the same bound as the upstream normalized-direction argument, with a division-free proof.

boundary: No existence or measurable selection of supporting vectors is claimed. The theorem does not require convexity once a global supporting vector is supplied, just as the corresponding upstream direction.
This is a native local port of the norm bound, not a bulk import of Optlib or a sampling convergence result.
units.lean_statement: A supplied global supporting vector of a globally G-Lipschitz objective has norm at most G.
units.lean_proof: Probe at x+v, compare the quadratic lower growth with Lipschitz upper growth, and separate the zero-norm case.

units.title: The actual subgradient steps telescope weighted objective gaps
units.statement: Let f be globally G-Lipschitz. For sequences x_k,v_k and nonnegative real steps a_k, suppose v_k supports f at x_k and x_(k+1)=x_k−a_k v_k for every k. For every comparator z and every N≥0, the weighted objective gaps obey the displayed bound, including the terminal squared distance.
assumptions: E is a real inner-product space with its associated norm. No completeness or finite-dimensionality assumption is imposed.
G is a nonnegative real Lipschitz constant and f:E→ℝ is globally G-Lipschitz.
SupportsAt f x v means f(x)+⟨v,z−x⟩≤f(z) for every z∈E. It supplies a genuine global supporting vector; no differentiability or totalized gradient is used.
x,v:ℕ→E and a:ℕ→ℝ. Each a_k≥0; each v_k supports f at x_k; the update x_(k+1)=x_k−a_k v_k is an exact equality.
z is any comparator in E, not a supplied minimizer. N is any natural number, including zero. There is no division by a step or horizon.

steps.title: Turn support into a gap estimate
steps.text: Use the supporting inequality at the comparator z and reverse the displacement. The norm bound is proved by the preceding theorem inside this proof; it is not a new hypothesis.
steps.lean: SupportsAt evaluated at z; inner_sub_right; norm_le_of_supportsAt.

steps.title: Expand the actual update
steps.text: The squared-distance identity is exact for the supplied recurrence. Multiplying the gap estimate by 2a_k is legitimate because the step is nonnegative; the squared subgradient term is at most a_k²G².

steps.title: Sum and cancel adjacent distances
steps.text: Sum the one-step inequality for k=0,…,N−1. Interior squared distances cancel, leaving the initial and terminal terms. The Lean induction performs exactly this finite telescope; the empty sum is the N=0 base case.

boundary: This exposes the stronger weighted intermediate estimate used by the upstream convergence proof. It does not assert monotonicity of function values or a last-iterate rate.
The source uses positive steps; allowing zero steps and N=0 here is an explicit division-free generalization, not a repair. No stochastic oracle, kernel or expected sampling cost is constructed.
units.lean_statement: Finite weighted-gap telescope for actual Lipschitz subgradient updates with nonnegative steps.
units.lean_proof: Prove the support gap and subgradient norm bounds, expand the actual squared-distance update, then telescope by induction.

units.title: A finite run contains a subgradient iterate with the convergence bound
units.statement: Under the same Lipschitz, support and exact-update assumptions, suppose every step is strictly positive and N>0. For any comparator z, some index i<N satisfies the displayed normalized best-iterate objective-gap bound.
assumptions: E is a real inner-product space with its associated norm. No completeness or finite-dimensionality assumption is imposed.
G is a nonnegative real Lipschitz constant and f:E→ℝ is globally G-Lipschitz.
SupportsAt f x v means f(x)+⟨v,z−x⟩≤f(z) for every z∈E. It supplies a genuine global supporting vector; no differentiability or totalized gradient is used.
x,v:ℕ→E; a:ℕ→ℝ with a_k>0; each v_k supports f at x_k; x_(k+1)=x_k−a_k v_k for every k.
N>0, so the finite index set is nonempty and the sum of its positive step sizes is strictly positive.
z is arbitrary. Neither attainment of the global infimum nor differentiability is supplied.

steps.title: Take a genuine finite minimum
steps.text: Choose i minimizing f(x_k) among k<N. This finite choice exists because N>0; it is not a default value of a totalized infimum.

steps.title: Compare the best gap to the weighted gaps
steps.text: Multiply each minimum inequality by a_k≥0 and sum. Apply the preceding actual-update telescope, then discard only the nonnegative terminal squared distance.

steps.title: Divide only on the positive domain
steps.text: The sum of positive steps over a nonempty finite range is positive. Dividing by twice that sum preserves the inequality and produces the claimed witness.
steps.lean: Finset.sum_pos; le_div_iff₀. No zero-step quotient is asserted.

boundary: The upstream theorem writes the best finite value as a real sInf over k+1 iterates. An actual minimizing index is equivalent on this nonempty finite set; N>0 corresponds to its k+1 horizon.
No claim is made about the last iterate, existence of subgradient selectors, asymptotic iterate convergence, stochastic selection, PBPS/SPHMC or sampling complexity.
These are reusable Optlib-source components placed beside Optimisation Chapter6; the complete Chewi chapter statement/route is not silently declared finished.
units.lean_statement: A positive finite subgradient run has a best index with the normalized objective-gap guarantee.
units.lean_proof: Choose a minimizing finite index, bound its gap by the weighted gaps, use the actual-update telescope, and divide by the proved positive total step.
